new_entities.name: Hybrid work
new_entities.quote: The hybrid work problem? Why you need places.

quotes.text: First, it's not a separate app you install. You don't go to a website, create an account, or learn a new interface. Places lives inside Outlook in Teams, showing up in your calendar and your chat.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies that Places is built into existing tools rather than another app.

quotes.text: The problem isn't the office itself. It's not that offices are bad. It's that you have no information about who's coming in and when.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the hybrid work problem as a lack of information, not of offices.

quotes.text: This is completely optional. Microsoft does not force you to share your location. You opt in and you decide whether your work plan is visible to your organization.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Addresses the privacy concern people have about location sharing.

quotes.text: Places doesn't just show you where desks are. It helps you sit near the people you work with most.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the collaboration value behind graph-based desk recommendations.

quotes.text: Here's the thing, places is not a booking tool. It's a coordination platform. It connects your calendar, your building and your colleagues into one system.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis in a few words.

chapters.title: Why hybrid office days go wrong
Room booking with photos and Copilot
Analytics, admin and the AI-powered workplace

takeaways: Microsoft Places lives inside Outlook and Teams and connects your calendar with the physical office, so people know who is coming in and where to sit.
Work plans, map-based desk booking, room booking with photos, automatic check-in and Nearby turn office days from guesswork into coordination, with presence sharing always opt-in.
Utilization analytics, auto-release policies and a web admin portal help facilities teams, and Places data feeds Copilot and Microsoft Graph for smarter in-office decisions.
hook: Hybrid work often means driving to the office only to find your team stayed home. This episode explains Microsoft Places for employees, IT admins and facilities teams: how work plans, desk and room booking, check-in and analytics inside Outlook and Teams take the guesswork out of office days.
